1. Project Overview

1.1 What is Narada?

Narada is a terminal-native personal DJ application being developed for Fedora Linux.

Its long-term goal is to behave like an intelligent music DJ that can understand the user's listening context, select appropriate tracks, manage a queue, and eventually perform intelligent transitions between songs.

The project is intended to combine practical software engineering with academic Deep Learning and Reinforcement Learning research.

Working name: Narada
DJ identity: Narada
Repository: https://github.com/haricodes2970/DJ-Narada
Local repository: /home/hari007/Music/DJ
Music library root: /home/hari007/Music

1.2 Intended user experience

The eventual application should support:

  • A terminal command named narada.

  • Interactive terminal-based DJ controls.

  • Music discovery within the user's existing local library.

  • Listening modes such as Hip-Hop, Desi, Workout, and Deep Focus.

  • Track selection and queue management.

  • Playback controls.

  • A pixel-art DJ avatar.

  • Audio visualization.

  • Beat-aware transitions and intelligent sequencing.

  • Eventually, an ML-based music understanding system and an RL-based DJ policy.

These are long-term goals. They are not all implemented yet.

1.3 Academic direction

Proposed academic title:

Narada: An Intelligent Music DJ Using Deep Learning and Reinforcement Learning

The research direction includes:

  1. Audio classification or music understanding using pretrained or fine-tuned models.

  2. A simulated DJ environment for training and evaluating an RL agent.

  3. Comparison against deterministic and other baseline DJ policies.

  4. Evaluation of track selection and sequencing quality.

No Deep Learning or Reinforcement Learning implementation has been added during the Phase 2 work described in this handoff.

8. Task 3 — Safe Music-Library Scanner

Status: APPROVED after several code-review and remediation rounds.

Task 3 introduced the security-critical native scanner.

8.1 Files involved

Added:

  • native/narada-scan.c

  • scripts/build-native.mjs

  • tests/library/native-scanner.test.ts

Modified:

  • src/library/scanner.ts

  • tests/library/scanner.test.ts

  • tests/node-builtins.d.ts

  • package.json

  • docs/PHASE_2_SPEC.md

The native build generates ignored binaries:

  • dist/native/narada-scan

  • dist/native/narada-scan-test

The production binary is built without NARADA_TEST_HELPER.

The test binary is compiled separately with -DNARADA_TEST_HELPER.

Test-only hooks are guarded by the compile-time macro and are not active in the production helper.

8.2 Why a native helper was required

The initial TypeScript-only scanner had a race:

  1. Validate a directory.

  2. Close the directory handle.

  3. Reopen or enumerate it by path.

An attacker or concurrent process could replace the path with a symlink between validation and traversal.

Node.js 22's built-in filesystem APIs did not provide the descriptor-relative directory traversal required to eliminate that race under the approved strict no-symlink requirement.

A narrowly scoped Linux C helper was therefore approved.

The project specification was adjusted to permit a checked-in Linux-specific native helper while retaining the no-third-party-dependency constraint.

8.3 Native traversal design

The helper uses Linux/POSIX filesystem operations, including:

  • open()

  • openat()

  • fdopendir()

  • readdir()

  • fstatat(..., AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)

  • fstat()

  • O_DIRECTORY

  • O_NOFOLLOW

  • O_CLOEXEC

The scanner:

  • Opens and validates the root.

  • Traverses using directory descriptors.

  • Skips symlinks before descent.

  • Opens child directories relative to their parent descriptors.

  • Validates opened objects using fstat().

  • Checks the root filesystem device and skips different-device directories.

  • Handles disappearing or inaccessible entries with warnings.

  • Continues processing siblings after recoverable failures.

  • Cleans up directory streams and file descriptors.

  • Does not write to the music library.

The root path is canonicalized by TypeScript before the helper opens it. O_NOFOLLOW applies to the final opened path component; the design does not claim to reject symlinks in every preceding root-path component.

8.4 Mandatory exclusion

The following path is always excluded:

/home/hari007/Music/DJ

Caller-provided exclusions extend the mandatory exclusion and cannot replace it.

The scanner uses component-aware matching so that DJ is distinguished from DJ-other.

If the scan root is the excluded directory or is nested inside it, the scanner must not scan that excluded tree.

The native traversal must never follow symlinks, even if their targets are inside the root.

8.5 Native output protocol

The helper emits newline-delimited JSON records for files and warnings.

TypeScript:

  • Spawns the helper with shell: false.

  • Passes paths through an argument array.

  • Parses output incrementally.

  • Enforces a 1 MiB record limit.

  • Bounds stderr to 64 KiB.

  • Rejects malformed or oversized records.

  • Terminates the helper on protocol violations.

  • Rejects results outside the canonical root.

  • Does not silently fall back to unsafe TypeScript traversal.

The generated helper is built before tests execute.

8.6 Critical test coverage

Tests cover:

  • Inside-root symlinks.

  • Outside-root symlinks.

  • Symlinked files and directories.

  • File replacement with symlink.

  • Directory replacement with symlink.

  • Disappearing files and directories.

  • Deterministic permission/read failure injection.

  • Hard links.

  • Mandatory exclusion and boundary behavior.

  • Malformed JSONL.

  • Oversized output.

  • Silent-helper timeout.

  • SIGTERM-ignoring helper requiring SIGKILL.

  • Production/test-helper isolation.

  • Actual readdir() returning NULL with errno = EIO.

The test-only readdir() wrapper is compiled only in the test helper. Production uses the real readdir() function.

The test verifies the actual caller-side error branch, warning path and message, and sibling recovery.

8.7 Subprocess cleanup

The scanner's protocol runner uses a bounded termination lifecycle:

  1. Mark the operation as terminating.

  2. Send SIGTERM.

  3. Wait through a 250 ms grace period.

  4. Escalate to SIGKILL if required.

  5. Wait for process closure within a bounded cleanup period.

  6. Clear timers and avoid duplicate settlement.

  7. Report an explicit cleanup failure if termination cannot be confirmed.

PID-based tests verify that silent and SIGTERM-ignoring helper processes have exited after the scan operation settles.

9. Task 4 — Bounded Audio Metadata Extraction

Status: Implementation reported complete; final source review pending. Do not treat as approved yet.

Task 4 adds metadata extraction without introducing catalog/search or playback behavior.

9.1 Files added or modified

Added:

  • src/library/metadata.ts

  • tests/library/metadata.test.ts

Modified:

  • src/library/types.ts

  • tests/node-builtins.d.ts

The implementation report says existing scanner, native helper, protocol, and CLI behavior were preserved.

9.2 Public contract

The proposed metadata API is:

probeTrack(filePath, options?): Promise<ProbeResult>

The types include:

  • Track

  • ProbeOptions

  • ProbeResult

The existing type definitions and Phase 2 spec must be checked before further changes. Do not assume the implementation report alone proves the exact API matches the approved contract.

Track identity and fallback

For a path that can be canonicalized and statted:

  • id is the canonical absolute path.

  • path is the canonical absolute path.

  • title defaults to the filename without its extension.

  • sizeBytes comes from filesystem metadata.

Metadata can include:

  • Artist.

  • Album.

  • Duration in seconds.

  • Format.

If canonicalization or stat fails, the function returns a warning without inventing track metadata.

If ffprobe fails after canonicalization and stat succeed, the fallback track is retained along with a warning.

9.3 ffprobe invocation

The implementation invokes ffprobe with an argument array:

ffprobe -v error -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <canonical-path>

It uses:

spawn(executable, args, { shell: false, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] })

No shell interpolation is used.

9.4 Metadata normalization

The implementation extracts metadata from ffprobe's JSON:

  • format.format_name → format.

  • format.tags.title → title, falling back to the filename-derived title.

  • format.tags.artist → artist.

  • format.tags.album → album.

  • Duration → only when finite and nonnegative.

  • File size → filesystem stat result.

Missing tags or invalid optional fields should not cause an otherwise usable track to be discarded.

9.5 Resource and output limits

Default limits:

  • Timeout: 5 seconds per file.

  • Maximum stdout: 1 MiB.

  • Maximum stderr: 64 KiB.

The options are configurable through ProbeOptions.

Reported failure cases include:

  • Missing executable.

  • Spawn error.

  • Nonzero exit.

  • Malformed JSON.

  • Invalid duration.

  • Timeout.

  • Stdout overflow.

  • Stderr overflow.

The implementation report states that these preserve fallback metadata whenever the path can be canonicalized and statted.

The child-process cleanup lifecycle is reported to use:

  • SIGTERM.

  • 250 ms grace period.

  • SIGKILL escalation.

  • Bounded cleanup.

  • Timer cleanup.

  • Exactly-once settlement.

  • Explicit cleanup-failure warnings when termination cannot be confirmed.

These claims must still be verified by source review.

9.6 Test strategy

The metadata tests use temporary helper scripts instead of relying on the system ffprobe binary or personal music files.

Reported test coverage includes:

  • Valid JSON normalization.

  • Canonical track IDs and paths.

  • Paths containing spaces and Unicode.

  • Missing tags and filename fallback.

  • Invalid duration.

  • Nonzero exit.

  • Missing executable.

  • Argument-array invocation and shell: false.

  • Stderr bounds.

  • Configurable timeout.

  • Stdout bounds.

  • Fallback metadata preservation.

The latest report says the focused suite has five tests, all passing.
